(b) The verifier process is node --test over both test files. The accept rule's "execution plan command exited 0" refers to its exit status, and expectedStdoutMatch applies to its reporter stdout. The source observes (a) only through the test assertions that run inside (b) (p17-direct-cli-observation). assertedReturnValue "Hello, world!" has no newline and must not weaken the exact stdout contract of (a) (p06-asserted-return-value, p07-two-observation-subjects).

statements.text: Proof shape for the behavior claim. The claim is proved by executing the CLI and observing its stdout. Four evidence roles stay distinct and bind the same current obligation: realization (the actual body of generated/hello-world.mjs), verifier artifacts (the actual bodies of both test files), verifier execution (the admitted native observation of the node --test run) and independent semantic assessment. File presence, path shape, a plausible script, a pass count, a declared expectation or an author claim does not prove the behavior. A verifier that passes against a weaker contract, such as trimmed or substring stdout or a missing status assertion, does not close the exact stdout-and-status obligation.

statements.text: Scope boundary. The request is to implement the complete selected source, so no source obligation may be dropped. The source asks for a minimal program, so scope is not widened. The source makes none of these a subject obligation: packaging, publishing, a bin entry or global install, release, deployment, CI configuration, localization, alternative greetings, logging, performance, or cross-platform launchers. The subject also takes on no builder or runtime concern: traversal, admission, event records, requirement or proof ledgers, retry control or continuation control. These exclusions belong to the product definition, and the owner may reprice them. They do not forbid incidental files that leave the defined behavior unchanged (p13-unconstrained-cli-aspects).

Terms for downstream stages. Project root: the directory the source's relative paths resolve against and the directory the tests run the CLI from; the source does not identify it (p08-project-root-and-cwd). CLI stdout contract: exact stdout "Hello, world!\n" with exit status 0 under the defined invocation. Component test and UAT test: the two source-fixed verifier artifacts that assert that contract from the component perspective and from the end user's perspective. Verifier execution: node --test over both test files. Execution plan: the declared command, args and expectations. Admitted evidence: native execution observations admitted by the runtime, distinct from any file the subject authors. observedTestPassCount and planSatisfied: named in the source but not defined (p05-accept-rule-terms).

Each Intent statement is supported by the quotations it cites, and this comparison found no source obligation lost or weakened. It found one imprecision. In the source order only the implementation design precedes the script; the test design follows the script and precedes the two test sources. s08-authority-relations states the exact order. This asset refines Intent in five places without changing its meaning. It separates the CLI exit status from the verifier exit status (s19-observation-subjects). It reads the result-replacement ruling as naming the result record and not the plan (s16-result-carrier-conflict). It states the exact bytes and equality semantics of the stdout contract (s02-cli-behavior). It carries all sixteen Intent pressures forward and resolves none of them. It adds three new ones: p14-no-installation-scope, p16-component-versus-uat and p17-direct-cli-observation. This comparison is author work, not the independent assessment.

Carries Product p09 and affects r04, r09, r10, r13 and r14. The source calls the interpreter "node" and process.execPath. Under node --test, process.execPath in a test is the node running the runner; that is Node runtime behavior, not a source fact. node:test and node --test require a Node version that includes the built-in runner. A count of 2 or more therefore does not show that the component test and the UAT test each ran and passed. Whether the reporter output of the bound node supplies that identification, and whether acceptance requires it, is not yet decided.

Carries Product p17 and affects r01, r02 and r17. The verifier's admitted observation holds reporter output, not the CLI's own stdout bytes, so r01 and r02 are observed only through test assertions. The builder's worksite-lifecycle policy allows declared outcome probes executed inside the worker turn. Carries Product p18 and affects r14. The source requires env in the observation. It does not say whether that means the full process environment or only the declared execution environment, or how sensitive values are handled.

Carries Product p20 and affects all candidates. The seven historical constructed files are proposals from a failed run. Among them, test-execution-plan.json pins expectedTestPassCount 2 and expectedStdoutMatch "fail 0". They are not admitted realization, verifier artifacts or execution evidence, and they satisfy no binding here. Whether their bytes are reused is a Design decision checked against the full source.

New. The only allowed proof template is built on command execution and observation. r05 to r08, r11 and r12 govern document content and cross-artifact relations, which execution cannot prove. Their bindings put content proof in independent semantic assessment over the actual bodies and use verifier execution only to corroborate that the declared paths and commands are the ones run. Whether this assignment satisfies the template, or needs a template the lifecycle owner has not declared, is unassessed.

New. A test that passes whatever the CLI prints is weaker proof than r01 and r02 require. The source requires strict assertions on the spawned actual script. It does not require executed counter-evidence, such as a mutation run showing each test fails against a non-conforming CLI. For now discrimination rests on semantic assessment of the test bodies. Whether executed discrimination evidence is required is unassessed.

New. Every candidate r01 to r17 is unimplemented and unproved. No current realization or verifier artifact has been bound, no command has run for the current lifecycle, and no assessment has been admitted. Each binding stays open until all four evidence roles bind it over the same basis. Readiness to construct is not fulfillment.

New. "The JSON command must be node." sits under an instruction that produces both JSON files. Its referent may be the plan's declared command, the recorded observed command, or both. Native execution may record the bound absolute node executable path, not the bare name node. Design must state how the declared "node" corresponds to the executed executable identity without weakening r13 or r14.

New. The design coverage rules require an implementation and a verifier target for each active obligation. r15 (a prohibition), r16 (an acceptance evaluation) and r17 (a separation constraint) have no single implementation artifact of their own. Design must bind each of them to the artifacts it constrains (plan, tests, admitted execution) or disclose the gap. It must not satisfy them by adding a subject-local acceptance or result file.

criteria.explanation: I reacquired the complete source member (digest ce602ce2... verified), the three current predecessors (c889664c..., c7c2c70c..., 744102b0... verified), the rubric (c77a38d6... verified) and the candidate (7ecd7b37... verified). Every sourceQuotes entry in the candidate is an exact substring occurring exactly once in the source (computed check: zero failures), and every predecessorStatementRef resolves in the Intent, Product or Requirements asset. Each candidate description of an existing file matches the actual bytes and digest. The conformance document has sections Declaration, Project Root, Source Surface, Execution Proof and Governed Artifacts, and its table omits test-execution-result.json. The implementation design cites the conformance document as authority. generated/hello-world.mjs is 41 bytes containing only process.stdout.write("Hello, world!\n");. Sections 1-5 of the test design correspond to commands 1-4 and the assertedReturnValue relation. Both tests import only node:test, node:assert/strict and spawnSync, spawn process.execPath with ["generated/hello-world.mjs"] and cwd new URL("../../", import.meta.url), and strictEqual on error, status 0 and exact stdout. The plan holds exactly the five source values. The candidate keeps the exact-byte stdout contract (s05, s09, s14), the plan values (s10), the source's exact verifier command (s12), both explicit authority relations (s07, s21) and the three accept conditions as necessary conditions only (s17). No source meaning is lost or weakened; the assertedReturnValue relation explicitly forbids trimming (s15). Additions beyond the source are disclosed as additions: the per-file runs, the direct probe and the appended conformance section. The wording '14 bytes Hello, world! and one line feed' in s05 and in the existing conformance document is loosely phrased (13 characters plus LF = 14 bytes). The quoted normative string itself is exact, so this is not material.

criteria.explanation: Artifact coverage: all seven source-required artifacts are targets, with the two test files as verifier targets. Command coverage: verifier-plan-node-test runs exactly the source's verifier args. It uses the only declared executable capability (/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/24.7.0/bin/node), relativeCwd '.', an empty environment equal to the declared capability environment, timeout 60000 (limit 120000) and grace 1000 (limit 1000). Four commands is within the limit of 32, and seven targets within 64. No command installs anything. cli-direct-probe runs generated/hello-world.mjs with no further argument and requires process_exit 0 and stdout_exact "Hello, world!\n". That directly realizes the conformance execution proof and the evaluator case (no arguments, status 0, exact stdout). The aggregate command carries exit 0 and test_pass_count >= 2. The per-file runs give separate component and UAT observations. Reading the test bodies shows that both tests spawn the actual constructed CLI through process.execPath with a project-root cwd and strict assertions, with no mock, stub, constant or trimming. They exercise the real application as the source requires. No prewritten result exists or is planned. Zero failures is enforced implicitly: node --test exits non-zero on any failing test, so the exit-0 predicate covers it. The design does not state that link, and it defers the 'fail 0' containment check to the Evidence stage (p27). Some substrate readiness lies outside this assessment's readable scope and stays unassessed residual, not proof: whether process_exit, test_pass_count and stdout_exact are admitted C2 predicate kinds, how C2 parses node 24.7.0's default reporter (p29), and C2 env normalization (p18). The test_pass_count floor hard-codes 2 instead of reading the plan's expectedTestPassCount, so plan/predicate drift is not mechanically prevented. It is consistent only while the plan stays unchanged.

No owner ruling confirms that test-execution-plan.json is retained as the plan carrier (p03). The correspondence between the plan's literal "node" and the executed absolute capability path is a design reading (p24).

The following are outside this assessment's readable scope and unobserved: that process_exit, test_pass_count and stdout_exact are admitted C2 predicate kinds; that C2 parses the pass count from node 24.7.0's default --test reporter output (p29); and which env entries C2 records and how it handles sensitive values (p18). Two questions are unassessed: whether this lifecycle disclosure belongs in the subject's governing document, and whether its wording 'this project authors no such file' prejudges the p02 projection option.

Nothing has executed. The project-root cwd resolution, process.execPath identity under the runner, the CLI's exact stdout and exit status, both test passes, per-file results and the 'fail 0' fragment are all unobserved (p07, p08, p09, p17). No executed counter-evidence shows that either test fails against a non-conforming CLI (p22). Whether identical mechanics fully satisfy the UAT role is unassessed (p16).

Command execution cannot prove document content, path consistency or authority relations. Those rest on independent semantic assessment of the actual bodies. Whether the behavior template is an adequate proof carrier for them is unassessed (p21).

component-test-file, uat-test-file and cli-direct-probe go beyond the source's single verifier command (p28). Whether the owner accepts them, and whether acceptance requires per-file proof (p15), is undecided.

The source does not constrain stderr, arguments, stdin, TTY behavior, package.json presence, the scope of the no-installation rule, or the meaning of sdlcComplianceScenario, workerExecutes and node_cli beyond their literal text (p13, p14, p19). These stay open, not solved.

Admitted native Evidence carries the observation. Retiring the source's entry for that path, or keeping it as a projection after execution, needs an owner ruling.

Carries Requirements p14. The design satisfies both the script-only reading and the whole-subject reading: no declared command installs anything, and the tests use only built-ins. Which reading governs is still undecided.

Carries Requirements p19. The design infers nothing from sdlcComplianceScenario, workerExecutes or kind node_cli beyond their literal text.

Carries Requirements p21. No command can prove document content or cross-document relations. The commands only corroborate the declared paths and proof path.

Carries Requirements p22. The design includes no mutation or negative run showing that either test fails against a non-conforming CLI. The direct probe is an observation independent of the tests. Discrimination rests on semantic assessment of the test bodies.
Carries Requirements p23. Every active obligation remains unproved. Construction, admitted execution, evidence binding and independent assessment are still owed, and readiness is not fulfillment.

New. The stage contract lists active requirement, obligation and version coordinates without candidate labels. The design maps them by position to candidates r01 to r17. If the order differs, the targets carry the wrong obligations, and the mapping must be corrected before construction.

New. component-test-file, uat-test-file and cli-direct-probe go beyond the source's single verifier command. They corroborate the source's command and do not replace it. Whether the owner accepts these additional executions has not been assessed.

New. The execution-evidence territory is available, but the design declares no report files, because the supplied contract does not name the report-identity vocabulary. Named per-test identities are therefore not bound by any predicate.

statements.text: Commands. The design declares four commands. All use the one executable capability /opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/24.7.0/bin/node with relativeCwd ".", an empty declared environment, no expected reports and a 1000 ms termination grace. (1) verifier-plan-node-test runs --test test/component/hello-cli.test.mjs test/uat/hello-cli.uat.test.mjs, the source's verifier with exactly the plan's args, with a 60000 ms timeout. (2) component-test-file runs --test test/component/hello-cli.test.mjs alone, with a 60000 ms timeout. (3) uat-test-file runs --test test/uat/hello-cli.uat.test.mjs alone, with a 60000 ms timeout. The plan keeps the source's literal command "node". The executed command identity is the bound absolute path, and comparing the plan with the execution treats "node" as naming that interpreter (p24). When that executable starts the runner, process.execPath inside each test file is the same executable, so each test spawns the CLI under the bound interpreter. statements.text: Outcome predicates. Eight predicates use existing C2 kinds. For verifier-plan-node-test: process_exit equals 0 and test_pass_count is at least 2. For component-test-file: process_exit equals 0 and test_pass_count is at least 1. For uat-test-file: process_exit equals 0 and test_pass_count is at least 1. For cli-direct-probe: process_exit equals 0 and stdout_exact equals "Hello, world!\n". The predicates declare what admitted execution must observe; they are not observations. A satisfied predicate is verifier-execution evidence only. It does not replace realization, verifier-artifact or semantic-assessment evidence, and it accepts nothing.

No existing C2 predicate kind expresses containment, and stdout_exact would pin volatile reporter text such as durations. The Evidence stage must therefore check the fragment against the admitted stdout of verifier-plan-node-test (p27). assertedReturnValue "Hello, world!" is the greeting text without the line feed. The design states its relation to the CLI this way: observed CLI stdout equals assertedReturnValue followed by exactly one "\n". The stdout_exact predicate "Hello, world!\n" on cli-direct-probe observes that relation. The relation never licenses a trimmed comparison (p06).

statements.text: Observation subjects. The design keeps the two processes separate at every point. The CLI process is observed directly by cli-direct-probe and indirectly by each test's assertions on the spawned result. The three --test commands observe the test-runner process. stdout_exact applies only to CLI stdout. The fail 0 fragment and the pass counts apply only to runner output. The accept rule's exit condition refers to the runner's exit status, and the tests' status assertion refers to the CLI's exit status.

statements.text: Acceptance. The design declares no acceptance artifact, because the source's acceptance stage produces no files. The accept rule's three conditions are evaluated over admitted observations of verifier-plan-node-test: its exit status, observedTestPassCount taken from the admitted pass-count observation, and planSatisfied. Without an owner ruling, the design proposes that planSatisfied means every plan expectation holds on admitted observations: exit 0, a pass count of at least expectedTestPassCount, reporter stdout containing expectedStdoutMatch, and CLI stdout equal to assertedReturnValue followed by "\n" (p05). The three conditions are necessary, not sufficient. An independent evaluator or owner rules on acceptance (p04), and the constructing worker cannot accept its own work.

gaps: All 17 active obligations are unproved. Each still needs admitted native execution of the four Design commands (verifier-plan-node-test, component-test-file, uat-test-file, cli-direct-probe) inside the worker turn, plus independent semantic assessment. I ran none of them because the instructions forbid it.
p01: an owner has not ruled whether the source's per-stage 'Write only' restrictions or its stage order bind construction. All seven targets were produced in one construction step.

p02: an owner has not ruled on the source-named test-execution-result.json. The path is neither retired nor kept as a derived projection. It has no target and was not written. The conformance document now states this.
p03 and p24: no owner has confirmed that test-execution-plan.json stays as the plan carrier, or that the plan's 'node' corresponds to the bound executable /opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/24.7.0/bin/node.

p04 and p05: the acceptor is unassigned, the sufficiency of the three accept conditions is undecided, and observedTestPassCount and planSatisfied have only Design-proposed definitions, not owner definitions.
p06: the relation between assertedReturnValue and the CLI (stdout equals it plus exactly one '\n') is a Design reading that no owner has confirmed.

p07, p27 and p29: the 'fail 0' fragment has not been checked against the actual Node 24.7.0 reporter output. No existing predicate checks containment, so the Evidence stage must check it. Pass-count parsing of that reporter's output has not been observed.
p08 and p09: the project-root cwd binding, and process.execPath being the same executable that runs the test runner, have not been observed.
p15, p17 and p28: per-file runs and the direct CLI probe are Design additions. The owner has not accepted them as corroborating executions.
p18: the env record scope and handling of sensitive values are unbound.

p13, p14, p16, p21, p22 and p25 remain unassessed or pending: unconstrained CLI aspects, no-installation scope, whether the UAT test needs anything beyond shared mechanics, proof of document content by assessment only, no executed discrimination or mutation evidence for the tests, and target coverage for the obligation-only requirements r15 to r17.

p26: I used the Design's position-based mapping from active coordinates to candidates r01 to r17, which no supplied artifact states. If that mapping is wrong, target obligation bindings need correction.
